Enacted a week after the September 11 attacks, this joint resolution authorizes the President to use all necessary and appropriate force against the nations, organizations, or persons that planned, authorized, committed, or aided the attacks, or that harbored those who did.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 107-40](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/107/public/40){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 50 U.S.C. 1541 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/1541?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 2(a): the operative grant of authority, tied to responsibility for the September 11 attacks.
- Sec. 2(b): declares the resolution to be specific statutory authorization under the War Powers Resolution.
- Contains no geographic limit, no named enemy, and no expiration date.

## Why it matters

Successive administrations have read it to cover al-Qaeda, the Taliban, and 'associated forces', and later the Islamic State, in countries far from Afghanistan. It also underpins wartime detention at Guantanamo, which links it to the [Detainee Treatment Act](dta-2005.qmd) and the [Military Commissions Act](mil-commissions-2006.qmd). Proposals to repeal or replace it recur in most Congresses.

## Current status

In force with no sunset. It survived the December 2025 repeal of the two Iraq authorizations and remains the main statutory basis for counterterrorism operations.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}

## In the courts

- [Hamdi](../cases/hamdi-2004.qmd) (2004). Held that the AUMF's authorization of necessary and appropriate force includes detention of enemy combatants captured in Afghanistan for the duration of hostilities.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [War Powers Resolution](wpr-1973.qmd), [Declarations of War](declarations-of-war.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [Military Commissions Act](mil-commissions-2006.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 50 U.S.C.](title50-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** After September 11 ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 3: Deciding to use force](../study/units/war-powers.qmd) (core reading); [Unit 12: Civilian harm and the conduct of operations](../study/units/civilian-harm.qmd) (further reading).
- **Member lenses.** [Rep. Jason Crow](../members/crow.qmd): Armed Services; Nigeria strikes briefing; Afghan Adjustment Act; Afghanistan TPS Act; Afghanistan oversight (2020). [Rep. Sara Jacobs](../members/jacobs.qmd): Foreign Affairs; Nigeria strikes briefing.
